program: Collective Legal Services; finite health effects of eviction defense

nutshell.headline: Legal representation can avert evictions; the local health bridge remains uncertain
nutshell.body: Signed prior-weighted estimate: $21,354,853 per 10 Bay QALYs (0.004683 Bay QALYs per $10,000). This is an exploratory whole-gift estimate, not measured EDC health outcomes.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: A focused law firm can preserve housing for vulnerable tenants who would otherwise lose it, with possible health benefits.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The favorable 10% world supplies 109.7% of signed expectation. Local causal eviction reduction, full-case share and finite utility remain uncertain. A share above 100% means the other scenarios have negative net expected health; it is not a probability.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: HOLD a giving recommendation: no verified current donation-created capacity or client health counterfactual. Preserve the unfavorable estimate rather than tuning it.

programSection.body: Collective Legal Services — Eviction Defense Center, EIN 94-3188860, serves Alameda County and Richmond tenants facing eviction. It is distinct from San Francisco Eviction Defense Collaborative. The dated return reports approximately 1,200 clients; the current undated website says over 2,000 and describes litigation alongside outreach and stabilization support.

steps.title: Use whole organization cost
steps.detail: Retain public-funded and privately funded operations, management and non-litigation work.

steps.title: Identify unique qualifying cases
steps.detail: Clients × household equivalence × qualifying representation share; no family or appearance multiplier.

steps.title: Apply causal eviction reduction
steps.detail: An explicit external-evidence transfer prior, not observed retention or material-benefit rates.

steps.title: Model finite signed health
steps.detail: Health-relevant share × utility × incremental duration, less harms, with funding response and Bay attribution.

programSection.boundary: Only health effects through avoided evictions are quantified. Housing security, due process, rent and debt relief, habitability work, economic gains and non-litigation support may matter but receive no extra QALY bonus. All costs remain. Donated labor, court resources and partner inputs are not fully priced. No mortality or lifetime extrapolation.

model.headline: $21,354,853 per 10 Bay QALYs
model.body: The historical client rate is not an offer to buy extra cases. The model separates cash response, qualifying service, legal effect and health effect to avoid treating every favorable settlement as a health gain.

equation.label: Signed incremental Bay housing health
equation.expression: gift / whole expense × clients × unique household factor × funding response × (representation share × causal eviction reduction × health-relevant share × utility × incremental years − harm per household) × Bay share

inputs.label: Whole calendar-2024 expense
inputs.basis: Original expense includes $1,589,609 program and $161,783 management; no grant, fee or investment-income subtraction.

inputs.label: Reported annual clients
inputs.basis: Dated filing approximately 1,200 clients; not 1,200 full trials, households or prevented evictions.

inputs.label: Unique household equivalence
inputs.basis: Accounts for repeated clients or co-clients in one household; credit one health beneficiary per household, not every family member.

inputs.label: Qualifying representation share
inputs.basis: Excludes brief advice and non-litigation contacts from the counsel causal bridge. Berkeley subset includes different service levels.

inputs.label: Absolute eviction reduction
inputs.basis: Transfer judgment, not local 65% retention. NYC executed-warrant estimates .084/.058 support scale, not direct transport to East Bay law or existing alternatives. Favorable .15 assumes higher-risk targeted clients.

inputs.label: Health-relevant share of avoided evictions
inputs.basis: Separates housing/legal success from health improvement. Eviction does not invariably cause homelessness or poor health.

inputs.label: Utility among health-affected beneficiaries
inputs.basis: Analyst judgment for temporary health improvement; hospital visits are not converted mechanically into QALYs.

inputs.label: Incremental health duration
inputs.basis: Expected time until alternative housing/support or need resolution catches up. Finite undiscounted exposure, no recurrence or lifetime benefit.

inputs.label: New-gift capacity response
inputs.basis: Separate budget response amid public contracts, staffing and reserves; no verified cash-priced additional case.

inputs.label: Bay health share
inputs.basis: Alameda County and Richmond footprint, not a complete residence census.

inputs.label: Harm QALY per additional household
inputs.basis: Independent assumed health loss from delayed escalation, unsafe housing retention or procedural error; not observed incidence and not already netted in utility.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Subjective scenario mass below $1M per 10: 0; below $100k: 0. Not calibrated probabilities. Excluding and renormalizing the favorable world gives Not defined per 10. Coefficients were locked before first calculation; no threshold tuning. Here the non-favorable scenarios have a negative signed expectation, so their cost per positive QALY is undefined—not zero cost or zero impact.
model.fundingBoundary: Original 2024 revenue is $2,249,592, including $1,278,549 government grants and $465,163 program revenue. Their detailed restrictions and whether program revenue includes contracts or fees are unverified. Whole expense is $1,751,392, including $1,328,429 staff costs. Cash $611,187 plus savings $1,302,388 equals $1,913,575 net assets, with zero reported liabilities; restriction status is not established by the return presentation. The Berkeley packet proposes existing contract continuation at $435,500 per year, not a marginal private funding gap. Its appended resolution has blank votes, so that packet alone does not prove execution. A gift may replace funding, support existing work or expand capacity; current allocation is unknown.

evidence.population: Approximately 1,200 clients across the whole firm
evidence.result: General legal-aid output, not exact unique households or full litigation cases.
evidence.transfer: Dated denominator chosen over undated website volume; no claim that clients are causal beneficiaries.

evidence.design: Provider report in Berkeley public contract packet
evidence.population: Berkeley subset, first 11 months of FY2025
evidence.result: Over 776 unduplicated tenants, over 96 unlawful-detainer actions, over 212 appearances; over 65% of cases resolved with tenants remaining home.
evidence.transfer: Service levels and periods differ. Retention is descriptive, not an absolute causal reduction; appearances are not people. No local QALYs measured.

evidence.population: Housing court cases; IV effect among induced representation compliers
evidence.result: Executed warrants: −8.4 percentage points (SE2.1) main IV; −5.8 (SE3.4) address-fixed-effects. Possessory judgments: −32.1 points, a different outcome.
evidence.transfer: Not a universal causal effect for all referrals. East Bay law, pandemic debt and existing counsel differ; local .06 remains judgment. No health outcome in this counsel paper.

evidence.design: Massachusetts District Court randomized representation offer
evidence.result: About two-thirds offered full representation retained possession versus about one-third of controls.
evidence.transfer: Small selected context, not population-wide health evidence; full versus limited service distinction matters.

evidence.design: Separate Massachusetts Housing Court randomized study
evidence.population: Full representation offer versus limited-assistance alternative
evidence.result: No statistically significant substantive outcome advantage was found.
evidence.transfer: Supports a legal null world and careful baseline comparison; do not conflate this court/study with the positive District Court trial.

evidence.design: Judge-leniency instrumental-variable study, Chicago and NYC
evidence.result: Eviction increased homelessness and hospital use over the following two years.
evidence.transfer: Supports a causal health pathway, not a QALY coefficient. No assumption every prevented eviction prevents homelessness; finite utility and duration are explicit priors.

reservations: Public funding and liquid assets do not prove zero marginal benefit, but undermine an assumed cash emergency.
Full-case and unique-household shares are not measured in the 1,200-client denominator.
65% retained housing is not 65 percentage points of causal benefit.
Legal outcomes and health outcomes require separate bridges.
One modeled beneficiary per household; no automatic child or family multiplier.
The two-year favorable duration is an assumption, not a measured local benefit period.
Harm and null worlds remain; long-run market/systemic effects are unquantified.
No donation route verified; donationUrl omitted.
excludedBenefits: Rent/debt relief counted again as QALYs
Unmeasured habitability and other support health gains
